problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ for the curve $r(t)=⟨t,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.$
worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-\operatorname{tan}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨1,-\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{tan}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-{sec}^{2}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨0,-{sec}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ and ${r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,-2,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-2\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖} \\  & =\frac{(\sqrt{2})^{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
